dates.notes: Launched by the President of the French Republic at the Internet Governance Forum at UNESCO and the Paris Peace Forum. The European Union and the United States joined on 11 November 2021. The supporters list is a current online list, not a dated depositary table; this record is a snapshot at 24 November 2026.

gaps: Non-binding: the Call creates no legal obligation, ratification, depositary, monitoring, reporting or enforcement.
The official supporters page is a dynamic list with no formal update log or depositary; the record is a snapshot at 24 November 2026 and later additions are not reflected.

Only the 81 State supporters and the European Union are recorded and mapped; the 36 public authorities, 390 civil-society organisations and 706 private-sector supporters reported by the official homepage are outside this State-level map.

The homepage counters and the official site's source data do not fully agree for non-State categories (public authorities, organisations and companies differ by one or two); the State count is 81 in both.
The European Union is a supporter but is not a State and is not shown on the State map.
No full text is stored; the official English and French texts are linked but not acquired.

languages.note: English and French are the two published language versions of the Call. The Call is not a treaty and has no authentic-language clause; only the English text was read.

legal_nature.rationale: A call opened to States, local governments, companies and civil-society organisations. It contains no signature, ratification, depositary, entry-into-force or enforcement clause; support is political endorsement, not legal obligation.

endorsements.note: 81 State entries plus the European Union, all read from the official supporter list. The official homepage separately counts 81 States.

notes: Participating international organisation, not a State; counted separately from the 81 States.

parties.summary: 81 States and the European Union are listed as supporters. The 27 EU member States are individually listed; the European Union is counted separately as an international organisation, not as a State.
unknowns: No formal depositary, membership procedure or public update log is published; the supporters page is the only current list.
The date on which each State or the European Union joined is not published on the supporters page.
The non-State supporter categories are not enumerated here; the official page counts them separately.

related.note: The Call describes the Budapest Convention as a key tool against cybercrime; it does not incorporate or amend it.

cyber_provisions: Principle 1 — prevent and recover from malicious cyber activities against individuals and critical infrastructure
Principle 2 — protect the public core of the Internet
Principle 3 — prevent malign interference with electoral processes
Principle 4 — prevent ICT-enabled theft of intellectual property
Principle 5 — prevent the proliferation of malicious ICT tools and practices
Principle 6 — strengthen the security of digital processes, products and services throughout their lifecycle and supply chain
Principle 7 — support advanced cyber hygiene for all actors
Principle 8 — prevent non-State actors, including the private sector, from hacking back
Principle 9 — promote international norms of responsible behaviour and confidence-building measures
relevance.excluded_scope: Non-binding political support; no legal obligations, monitoring or enforcement. Only State-level supporters and the European Union are mapped; companies, civil society and local authorities are outside the map.
relevance.reason: A multistakeholder non-binding cyber declaration launched by France in 2018. It is the first non-binding cyber instrument in the corpus with an official, downloadable State-level supporter list, so it is catalogued and mapped as political endorsement, not as a treaty.
